section_summary: This section describes Japanese military, naval, police and civilian intelligence organizations operating in China and Manchuria. Its exhibits cover the Kwantung Army, several Peiping organizations, intelligence work in Tsingtao, and a South China espionage network. The final report, continuing beyond page 273, examines the Japanese Foreign Office, its personnel and consulates, and the Asia Development Board.

subfiles.title: Kwantung Army Intelligence Service
subfiles.about: The Kwantung Army's intelligence organization and its methods for gathering information on Soviet forces.
subfiles.summary: Describes the Second Section's organization, radio decoding, aerial photography, patrols, diplomatic reporting, interrogations and agents. It judges cross-border espionage ineffective and distinguishes military intelligence from police and peace-preservation work.

subfiles.title: The 3rd Independent Guard Unit, Peiping
subfiles.about: Intelligence work against Chinese Communist forces by an independent guard unit in the Peiping area.
subfiles.summary: Outlines the unit's staff, planned training, information sources and mixed operational results, including a reported success at Huinchen-hsien.

subfiles.title: Peiping Information Organ (Shigekawa Organ)
subfiles.about: The Shigekawa Organ's contacts, agents, expenses and political activities in North China.
subfiles.summary: Describes information gathered through Muslim contacts and Chinese acquaintances, work during the Honan operation, and unsuccessful attempts to arrange political and peace contacts.

subfiles.title: Peiping Special Intelligence Corps
subfiles.about: The corps' organization, radio interception, codebreaking and direction-finding results.
subfiles.summary: Lists personnel and equipment and compares success against Chinese radio networks. The corps deciphered some routine or propaganda traffic but failed against important Communist operational codes; direction finding was generally unsatisfactory.

subfiles.title: Hidaka Organ
subfiles.about: The Hidaka Organ's foreign-intelligence contacts and assessment of its effectiveness.
subfiles.summary: Identifies its Peiping and Tientsin offices and describes information gathered through foreign residents, diplomats, publications and radio interception. The source judges its results poor relative to its staffing.

subfiles.title: Functions and Personnel of the Hidaka Organization
subfiles.about: A detailed account of the Hidaka organization's assignments, collection network, training and evaluation practices.
subfiles.summary: The exhibit describes orders from North China Army headquarters, wireless reception units, foreign news monitoring, immigrant associations and German correspondents used as information sources. It also covers agent contact methods, staff education, spending, and Hidaka's personal assessment of reports. Its closing pages discuss delays and errors in evaluating information.

subfiles.title: Japanese Intelligence Agencies in Tsingtao
subfiles.about: Army, Navy and gendarmerie intelligence and counter-intelligence operations in Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: Traces organizational changes from the 1938 occupation through 1945 and separates combat, general and counter-intelligence work. It describes censorship, surveillance of foreign residents, Chinese and civilian informants, and poor security and cooperation among Japanese agencies.

subfiles.title: Japanese Espionage System in South China
subfiles.about: Chart of Japanese espionage organizations, commands and liaison links in South China.
subfiles.summary: Maps intelligence organizations and their supervisory or liaison links across South China.

subfiles.title: Japanese–South China Intelligence Group Five Provinces Information Department
subfiles.about: A Japanese-sponsored South China espionage group's leadership, mission, recruitment, training and communications.
subfiles.summary: Describes the group's creation, Canton headquarters and branches, named leaders, military reporting priorities, agent recruitment and training. It also records pay, commercial and medical covers, courier methods, finances and examples of product-based codes.

subfiles.title: Kempei Tai at Tsingtao, North China
subfiles.about: Gendarmerie intelligence sections and the Matsuda Battalion's anti-Communist activities around Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: Outlines the gendarmerie's sections and the Matsuda Battalion's infiltration and interrogation work.

subfiles.title: Japanese Civilian Organizations in Intelligence
subfiles.about: The Japanese Foreign Office, diplomatic intelligence personnel and the Asia Development Board's work in China.
subfiles.summary: The report begins with a contents page and introduction, then traces Foreign Office organization and responsibilities before, during and after the Greater East Asia Ministry. It discusses military and naval attachés, Shanghai embassy financial and intelligence staff, Russian-affairs informants, and the distribution of embassies and consulates in China. Its final pages in this section describe the Asia Development Board's origins, senior personnel and liaison offices; the report continues beyond page 273.
